q-102535.name: Question 2
q-102535.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227428/assets/f498fdcd8c6be58b8d1c1e6e4c3d835799a8c571cdd9125f7e7555307c94a6d1.png)

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?

I. ${lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}f(x)=\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}f(x)=\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to 3}f(x)=1$
q-102535.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the limits in question.

We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $3$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $\infty .$ So, the left-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}f(x)=\infty \,.
$$

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $3$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $\infty .$ So, the right-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}f(x)=\infty \,.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{lim}_{x\to 3}f(x)=\infty \,.
$$

Now, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true.

- Statement II is true.

- Statement III is false.

In conclusion, statements I and II are true.

q-35921.name: Question 3
q-35921.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227428/assets/fc6f40458a9a38615b9d1fe01c7e454611a56915d2dcaadaa8661c4d56defb6f.png)

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?

I. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=\text{DNE}$
q-35921.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the limits in question.

As $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty ,$ and therefore

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

As $x$ approaches $1$ from the left, the function is not defined. So we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

Now, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true.

- Statement II is false.

- Statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statements I and III are true.
